title: How login works in shop-api
goal: From typing an email and password to calling an API that needs login, and renewing the token (a made-up sample project)

glossary.access token: A short-lived JWT (15 minutes) sent with every request to say who you are
glossary.refresh token: A long-lived code (14 days) used to get a new access token without typing the password again

steps.title: User sends email + password
steps.detail: The web page sends POST /auth/login with the email and password; the route checks the format before passing it on
steps.done: You know what comes in, and what is rejected at the front door

steps.title: Check the password
steps.detail: authService finds the user by email and compares the password with the hash using bcrypt; every failure gets the same answer
steps.done: You can say why the real password is never stored, and why every failure looks the same

steps.title: Issue two tokens
steps.detail: Issue an access token (JWT, 15 minutes) and a refresh token (14 days, kept in Redis) and send both to the web page
steps.done: You can say how the two differ and where each is kept

steps.title: Call the API with the token
steps.detail: Every request carries the access token; the requireAuth middleware checks its signature and expiry before the handler runs
steps.done: You know an expired token gets a 401, and who checks it

steps.title: Renew the token
steps.detail: On a 401 the page sends the refresh token to /auth/refresh, gets a new access token, and the old refresh token is revoked
steps.done: You can say why the old one is revoked every time

web.name: Web page
web.out: Access token in memory, refresh token in an httpOnly cookie
web.why: Outside this repository, but it starts everything

route.name: auth routes
route.out: Calls authService, or answers 400 if the format is wrong
route.why: Checking the format at the front door keeps junk out of the code behind it

service.name: authService
service.in: Email and password, or a refresh token
service.out: Access token (JWT, 15 min) + refresh token (14 days)
service.why: Security rules live in one place: the same answer for every failure, and a new refresh token every time

repo.name: userRepo
repo.why: Fetches no other columns, so less personal data passes through

pg.name: PostgreSQL
pg.why: Stores a hash, not the real password

redis.name: Redis
redis.out: Accepts or rejects it on renewal
redis.why: Can revoke a token at once, unlike a JWT that lives until it expires

guard.name: requireAuth
guard.why: Every route that needs login goes through this one place

orders.name: orders handler
orders.why: Always uses req.user.id, never an id sent in the body
